segments.text: His leg is broken. He's hanging off a cliff in the dark. Then the rope goes slack.
He drops into a crevasse and lands on a ledge of ice.
He can't climb out. The ice overhangs, and his leg is useless. So he lowers himself deeper, into the dark.
Down there, a slope of snow leads up to daylight.
Then he crawls and hops for days, across the glacier and the rocks below it. No food. Almost no water.
He reaches camp hours before his partner was due to leave.
That partner, Simon Yates, had been lowering him down the mountain on a rope. In a storm he held his weight until his own seat in the snow gave way. Then he cut the rope.
Joe Simpson always defended him. He said he would have done the same.
I was wrong. He lived, and so did the man who cut it. Would you have cut the rope?
